best_outcome.summary: Cross into Battahl, recover the Letter to Lord Phaesus from the Forbidden Magick Research Lab and bring it back to Sven.
steps: Speak to Sven in Vernworth Castle to take the quest.
Oxcart west to Checkpoint Rest Town.
If you are not Beastren, buy a Beastren Mask from Ibrahim's Scrap Store (8,700G).
Show the permit at the Vermund-Battahl border checkpoint.
Follow the markers to the Forbidden Magick Research Lab.
Take the Letter to Lord Phaesus and return it to Sven in Vernworth.

bad_outcome.summary: The quest is lost rather than failed.
bad_outcome.how_it_happens: Triggering 'Legacy' and entering the Unmoored World with the quest unfinished.
bad_outcome.consequences: Quest deleted; XP, 20,000G and the Dragon Ferrystone are forfeited for the run.

along_the_way: Expect ambushes on the road to the research lab; clearing them is required to proceed.
gotchas: Sources conflict: Game8's quest page states no timing constraints or missability, while Fextralife's master list flags it as lost at Legacy. Fextralife is treated as authoritative here.
'Masked Correspondence' is itself deleted by Feast of Deception, so it must be finished BEFORE Feast of Deception or this quest can never unlock.

name: Beren's Final Lesson
how_to_start: Speak to Beren at Moonglow Garden after completing 'Claw Them Into Shape'. A cutscene triggers automatically on approach.
prerequisites: Complete 'Claw Them Into Shape'.
timing: Immediately after Claw Them Into Shape. Beren relocates to Beren's Childhood Home once this begins.

missable.warning: Not flagged missable, but it gates the Warrior maister skill Arc of Might. Do it before the Unmoored World transition.

bring: Anti-Cyclops kit: knockdown/stagger tools, ladder-climbing melee

best_outcome.summary: Kill the Cyclops alongside Beren and his trainees, then rest a full in-game day and return to Beren for the reward and the Warrior maister skill.
steps: Fight the Cyclops with your pawns and Beren's charges.
Wait a full in-game day (campfire nearby works).
Return to Beren.
rewards: Arc of Might — Warrior maister skill, taught by Beren on questline completion

gotchas: The day-wait is mandatory; people report thinking the quest is bugged when it just needs a rest.
Arc of Might is learned by talking to Beren after the questline, at approx. world-map coords X:4616 Y:6531 — verify in-game, single source.

name: Brothers Brave and Timid
how_to_start: Speak to Ian in Melve, near Lennart's house, after reaching Melve in the early game. He asks for help finding his brother Norbert.
prerequisites: Reach Melve in the early game (after 'Seat of the Sovran' per Game8).
timing: Early Vermund, while Melve is still intact and before the Vernworth main story reaches Feast of Deception.

missable.window: Closes permanently when the main quest 'Feast of Deception' is completed.
missable.warning: Do this in Melve before you finish Feast of Deception in Vernworth - once that quest ends the brothers' questline is deleted for good.

bring: A Mage or Archer pawn for ranged support and healing on the escort

best_outcome.summary: Follow Ian into the woods, save Norbert from wolves, and bring both brothers home alive.
steps: Talk to Ian by Lennart's house in Melve and accept.
Follow Ian north-west out of Melve toward Backwoods Nest Cave.
Kill the wolves attacking Norbert quickly - he is fragile.
Escort both brothers back to Melve and report in.

bad_outcome.summary: Norbert (or Ian) dies during the rescue or escort.
bad_outcome.how_it_happens: The wolves kill Norbert before you reach him, or he is killed on the walk back to Melve.
bad_outcome.consequences: The brothers are no longer available to distract the storeroom guard during 'Home Is Where the Hearth Is', making that quest harder (you must fight, buy the swords yourself, or find another route).

along_the_way: Backwoods Nest Cave sits north-west of Melve on the route the brothers take.
gotchas: Game8 words the deadline as 'missable after visiting Vernworth for the first time' because that is what pushes the story toward the point of no return; Fextralife's master list states the hard cutoff as Feast of Deception. Treat Feast of Deception as the real wall and do the quest as early as possible either way.
Deaths here are not automatically fatal to the chain - a Wakestone revival is the usual community workaround, but no source confirms it restores the guard-distraction behaviour.

name: Civil Unrest
how_to_start: In the Unmoored World, Menella (also written Manella) approaches you automatically at the Bakbattahl oxcart station once 'Halls of the First Dawn' is available/started.
prerequisites: Be in the Unmoored World with 'Halls of the First Dawn' started. Menella must be alive. Empress Nadinia must have been saved during 'Shadowed Prayers' for her to appear at the end.
timing: Post-game only, inside the Unmoored World. One of the five regional evacuation quests required for the true 'Hero' ending.

missable.window: The Unmoored World allows roughly 10 days of rest before the world is destroyed; days advance only when you sleep. Separately, completing 'When Wills Collide' ends the game and closes all evacuations, and completing 'Halls of the First Dawn' lets you end the game at any time. The quest is also permanently blocked if Menella or Nadinia died before or during the Unmoored World.
missable.warning: Do all five evacuations before you finish 'Halls of the First Dawn' / 'When Wills Collide', sleep as little as possible, and make sure Menella and Nadinia are alive — dead leaders cannot be evacuated.

bring: Non-rotten fruit for the marketplace dispute
Wakestones, in case you need to revive Menella or Nadinia at the Morgue

best_outcome.summary: Break up three brawls across Bakbattahl, report to Menella, then get the Empress to agree to evacuate the city.
steps: Talk to Menella at the Bakbattahl oxcart station in the Unmoored World.

Resolve three separate fights around the city. PowerPyx says peaceful or violent methods both work; Game8 details them as enduring a brawl with aggressive citizens, settling a marketplace dispute, and witnessing a duel at the Vocation Guild.
For the marketplace dispute, pick the dialogue option 'Neither of you are wrong' and hand over non-rotten fruit.
Report back to Menella.
Go to Flamebearer Palace and speak with Empress Nadinia, who agrees to evacuate Bakbattahl's population.

bad_outcome.summary: Bakbattahl is never evacuated, costing you the true ending's best state.
bad_outcome.how_it_happens: Running out of Unmoored World days, ending the game via 'When Wills Collide' first, or having Menella or Nadinia dead. Game8 notes that failing to complete Menella's quest before triggering the red beam in that region can get her killed.
bad_outcome.consequences: The evacuation cannot be completed; Bakbattahl's population is lost and the 'Hero' / true-ending requirements go unmet for that region.

along_the_way: PowerPyx notes the Unmoored World trials should be completed without dying for 'The Hero' ending requirements.
Defeating the optional Purgener bosses extends the time you can spend in the Unmoored World (Dot Esports).
Dead NPCs can sometimes be revived with Wakestones at the Morgue.
gotchas: SOURCES CONFLICT on quest order. PowerPyx says Civil Unrest becomes available after STARTING 'Halls of the First Dawn'; Game8 says after COMPLETING it; Game8's Unmoored World overview instead recommends doing all five evacuations BEFORE 'Halls of the First Dawn'. Not resolved here.
SOURCES CONFLICT on the gold reward: PowerPyx 10,000 G, Game8 20,000 G. PowerPyx additionally lists 30 Wyrmslife Crystals that Game8 does not.
The NPC's name is written 'Menella' by PowerPyx and 'Manella' by Game8 — same character.
Nadinia only appears for the final report if you saved her during 'Shadowed Prayers'; otherwise Menella handles it.
Dot Esports could not confirm any per-quest deadline within the Unmoored World, only the overall ~10-day rest budget. No source gives a hard day count for Bakbattahl specifically.

name: Clash and Conclusion
how_to_start: Triggers automatically as you ascend Moonglint Tower during the stretch between the main quests 'The Guardian Gigantus' and 'Legacy' — but ONLY if you completed 'Tensions on the Highroad' beforehand. Raghnall blocks a narrow corridor and challenges you to a duel.
prerequisites: Complete 'Tensions on the Highroad'. That quest in turn is deleted by the main quest 'A New Godsway', so it must be done well before this point.
timing: Between The Guardian Gigantus and Legacy.

missable.window: Cancelled if you have not picked it up before starting the main quest 'Legacy'. It is also unobtainable outright if 'Tensions on the Highroad' was never completed — and Tensions is itself deleted by 'A New Godsway'.
missable.warning: This quest is gated two steps back: if you let A New Godsway delete Tensions on the Highroad, Clash and Conclusion can never appear, and even with Tensions done it is cancelled the moment you start Legacy.

bring: Grappling-capable build or a Thief/Warrior able to pin, if you want the non-lethal ending
A Wakestone if you intend to revive Raghnall afterward

best_outcome.summary: Beat Raghnall by grappling/pinning him without killing him, so he departs alive — this is the richest branch.
steps: Ascend Moonglint Tower after The Guardian Gigantus.
Raghnall challenges you to a one-on-one duel. Your pawns honour it and will not intervene.
Subdue him by grappling and pinning rather than landing the killing blow.

bad_outcome.summary: Killing Raghnall pays noticeably less and removes him from the world; fleeing pays least.
bad_outcome.how_it_happens: Defeating Raghnall lethally ends the duel with his death (7,600 XP and 15,000 G). Fleeing through the gate behind him is a third, poorest branch. Never triggering the quest at all — because Tensions was lost or Legacy was started first — loses everything.
bad_outcome.consequences: Killing him forfeits the Moonglint Key, The Exalted, and the larger 20,000 G payout. He can be revived with a Wakestone, but Game8 notes revival confers no benefit.

along_the_way: The duel corridor is deliberately narrow; ranged play is awkward, which is part of why the grapple route is viable.
gotchas: CLAIM NOT CONFIRMED: the brief says this 'requires Tensions on the Highroad AND siding with Raghnall; the other branch loses it.' Both Fextralife and Game8 state only that Tensions on the Highroad must be completed — neither conditions Clash and Conclusion on which side you took. Fextralife's Tensions page marks that quest 'Multiple Outcomes: No' and says 'you will pursue Raghnall either way', with the side-choice affecting only Raghnall's affinity. I could NOT verify the siding requirement and could NOT disprove it either; I have left it out of prerequisites and recorded it here.

SOURCE CONFLICT on outcomes: Fextralife documents three branches (kill / non-lethal departure / flee); Game8 presents it as a straightforward 'defeat Raghnall' with a single reward set. The three-branch version is the more detailed and the one worth guiding toward.
Fextralife lists the 'flee' branch rewards as still pending/unknown.

name: Claw Them Into Shape
how_to_start: Speak to Beren, the beastren Warrior Maister. He is first encountered at Borderwatch Outpost; the quest is taken at Moonglow Garden, southwest of Borderwatch Outpost.
prerequisites: Progress to the main quest 'In Dragon's Wake'. Some sources say you must speak to Beren at Borderwatch Outpost first.
timing: Available from early-mid Vermund once 'In Dragon's Wake' is active.

missable.warning: No source flags this as missable, but it is NOT in the Unmoored World, so finish it before the point of no return at Moonglint Tower / 'Legacy'. Treat that as the hard backstop.

bring: ~2,550 G for three training swords (850 G each at Borderwatch Outpost), or three swords from loot

best_outcome.summary: Deliver a willing soldier and three swords, then beat Beren in the sparring match; the questline continues into Beren's Final Lesson and eventually the Warrior maister skill.
steps: Find the motivated soldier: Humphrey, in Vernworth near Clovis's Barberie. Direct him to Beren.
Procure three swords (buy at Borderwatch Outpost, 850 G each, or supply looted ones).
Return to Beren at Moonglow Garden with the soldier and the weapons.
Spar with Beren. Win by knocking him OUT of the fighting area, not by killing him.
Goblins attack; follow Beren toward the encampment.
Reach the marked spot and find the wounded soldier.

along_the_way: Borderwatch Outpost also hosts 'The Provisioner's Plight' and 'Ordeals of a New Recruit' — the latter is timed, see its entry.
gotchas: The spar is a ring-out, not a kill. Do not try to burst him down.
Humphrey's location is the most common sticking point; he is in Vernworth, not at the outpost.
No source titles Beren a 'commander' — he is 'the Warrior Maister'.

name: Crossing in Shadow
how_to_start: Return to your own house in Vernworth at NIGHT after completing the main quest 'A Candle in the Storm'. A cutscene triggers with Vera, an attendant to Empress Nadinia of Battahl.
prerequisites: Own a house in Vernworth (bought for 20,000 G during 'A Place to Call Home') AND have completed 'A Candle in the Storm'.
timing: Night-time only, at your Vernworth house, once both prerequisites are met.

missable.window: Fextralife flags this quest (!) as missable. The confirmed, sourced way to lose it permanently is in-quest failure: blowing Nadinia's cover during the escort fails the quest and jails you, and it does not become re-offerable. I could NOT find a sourced story beat that deletes the quest before you start it — it is not on any of the three points-of-no-return lists (Feast of Deception / A New Godsway / Legacy). Treat the precise pre-start closing trigger as UNVERIFIED.
missable.warning: Once the escort starts you get one attempt — help the fleeing beastren or otherwise expose the Empress and you are thrown in gaol and the quest is failed for good.

bring: At least 1,000 G on hand for the medicine
Nothing else — your pawns are left behind for the whole escort

best_outcome.summary: Escort the disguised Empress Nadinia across Vernworth to the Rose Chateau without exposing her identity.
steps: Trigger the cutscene with Vera at your Vernworth house at night.
Begin the escort south through the city toward Rose Chateau Bolderie; your pawns stay behind.
A dialogue scene plays at the statue of the Arisen in the town square — answer without revealing who she is.
When the shopkeeper Philbert asks about medicine, pay the 1,000 G. Sources identify this as the best-outcome choice.
When a fleeing beastren begs for help while a soldier chases him, REFUSE. Helping him fails the quest.
Deliver Nadinia to Rose Chateau Bolderie to complete the escort.

bad_outcome.summary: Nadinia's identity is exposed, guards take you, and the quest ends in failure.
bad_outcome.how_it_happens: Helping the pursued beastren when he asks, or picking dialogue during the escort that gives away who your companion is, or drawing a guard pursuit.
bad_outcome.consequences: You are thrown into gaol and the quest is failed. You forfeit the 20,000 G, the Sunbloom and the XP, and you then have to break out of or buy your way out of jail.

along_the_way: The escort route passes the Arisen's statue in the town square, which has its own dialogue beat.
After the escort, Nadinia departs for Bakbattahl, which lines up with her later appearances in the Battahl main line.
gotchas: Your pawns are removed for the whole escort — you are effectively solo.
PowerPyx notes a spawn bug on lower-end PCs during the escort; jogging rather than sprinting avoids it.
Sources disagree on missability: Fextralife marks it (!), while PowerPyx and Game8 list no missable warning at all. Recorded here rather than resolved.
No source I could reach lists the exact dialogue option strings for the statue scene — only the outcome rules.

name: Dulled Steel, Cold Forge
how_to_start: Speak to Roman in the Vernworth Castle courtyard after completing 'Seat of the Sovran'; he asks you to follow him somewhere private and hands over the Dulled Regalia Sword.
prerequisites: Complete the main quest 'Seat of the Sovran'. Completing it requires access to Battahl (Bakbattahl / Brokkr's Smithy).
timing: Available from Chapter 1 after Seat of the Sovran, but cannot be finished until you can reach Bakbattahl.

missable.window: Lost permanently on starting the main quest 'Legacy' (entering the Unmoored World). Per Fextralife's master list this is one of the 13 side quests deleted at that point.
missable.warning: Finish this before you start Legacy — entering the Unmoored World deletes it outright, along with the 35,000 G payout and the Steeled Resolve, Blazing Forge follow-up.

bring: 15x Glimmercoal (from Digger's Ruins)
Combat gear able to clear the Mountain Base Cave path

best_outcome.summary: Get the Regalia Sword reforged by Sara and return it restored to Roman.
steps: Take the Dulled Regalia Sword to Brokkr's Smithy in southwestern Bakbattahl. Brokkr refuses; his apprentice Sara volunteers.
Collect 15x Glimmercoal from Digger's Ruins and give it to Sara.
Sara leaves for the natural forge at Mountain Base Cave, southwest of Geyser Hamlet. Clear the wooden-plank path there FIRST.
Escort Sara back before 'the hammer cools off' — this leg is on a timer.
Return the Restored Regalia Sword to Roman in Vernworth.

bad_outcome.summary: No alternate-completion branch exists; the failure mode is letting the escort timer run out, or losing the whole quest at Legacy.
bad_outcome.how_it_happens: Failing to escort Sara back in time during the Mountain Base Cave leg, or starting Legacy with the quest still open.
bad_outcome.consequences: Losing the quest at Legacy also forfeits 'Steeled Resolve, Blazing Forge', which is itself a prerequisite chain toward the Ailing Arborheart line.

along_the_way: Digger's Ruins is the reliable Glimmercoal source.
Clear the Mountain Base Cave plank path before triggering Sara's trip so the timed escort is uncontested.
gotchas: Fextralife's quest page says 'no time limit on overall quest completion' — that refers to the escort leg only and does NOT contradict the master list's Legacy cutoff.
There is no choice of blacksmith; Sara is the only path.
sources: Fextralife master side-quest list (Legacy cutoff group)

name: Every Rose Has Its Thorn
how_to_start: After 'The Stolen Throne' and 'An Unsettling Encounter', visit Wilhelmina at Rose Chateau Bordelrie. Sleep at an inn until morning, return to find Rolf guarding a room, then peek behind the painting in Wilhelmina's quarters to trigger it.
prerequisites: Complete 'The Stolen Throne' and 'An Unsettling Encounter'.
timing: PatchCrazy reports a strict THREE-DAY timer from the trigger cutscene. Must be done before heading to Battahl.

missable.window: Approximately 3 in-game days from the hidden cutscene trigger; also lost by progressing to Battahl / the Unmoored World.
missable.warning: BLUNT: THREE IN-GAME DAYS. Miss it and Wilhelmina GOES TO JAIL, the romance is dead, and it is locked until New Game+. Do not start this quest and then wander off to explore.

bring: Escape route planning — killing Allard alerts the guards and you must run, not fight

best_outcome.summary: Gather the evidence, present it, restrain Allard, escape the guards, and return to Wilhelmina the next morning.
steps: Speak to Sven in Vernworth Castle.
Visit Patrick's Estate at night.
Retrieve the Murder Report from Allard's manor.
Present the evidence to Wilhelmina.
Restrain Allard when he confronts her.
Escape the pursuing guards — avoid combat.
Return to Rose Chateau Bordelrie the next morning.

bad_outcome.summary: Letting the timer run out.
bad_outcome.how_it_happens: Not completing within the window, or progressing the main story to Battahl/Unmoored World first.
bad_outcome.consequences: Wilhelmina goes to jail. The Wilhelmina romance is permanently lost for the save.

gotchas: The trigger is finicky: one inn sleep may not fire it. Sleep additional days or do other tasks and come back.
Allard's death alerts guards — fighting them is the trap; running is the intended solution.
The exact '3 days' figure is SINGLE-SOURCE (PatchCrazy). Game8 confirms it is time-sensitive but does not state a number. Treat 3 days as a working assumption, not gospel.

name: Gift of the Bow
how_to_start: Speak to Glyndwr near Roderick's Smithy in Vernworth and give him any human-made bow. Bows made by elves or other races are refused.
prerequisites: You must be able to demonstrate archery during the training step — Archer, Magick Archer or Warfarer vocation.
timing: Available once you have reached Vernworth and can obtain or buy a human-made bow.

missable.window: Permanently deleted on entering the Unmoored World via the main quest 'Legacy'.
missable.warning: Finish this and its follow-up 'A Trial of Archery' before 'Legacy' — it is the only route to the Archer maister skill Heavenly Shot.

bring: A human-made bow (a cheap shop bow from Vernworth is fine)

best_outcome.summary: Hand Glyndwr a human-made bow and train with him, unlocking 'A Trial of Archery'.
steps: Speak with Glyndwr at Roderick's Smithy and give him a human-made bow.
Travel northwest past Trevo Mine to his training spot.
Help him train — demonstrate archery yourself.
Return to Vernworth and speak to him again near the smithy to open 'A Trial of Archery'.

bad_outcome.summary: Quest never started or abandoned before Legacy.
bad_outcome.how_it_happens: Entering the Unmoored World without completing it, or never finding Glyndwr at the smithy.
bad_outcome.consequences: Quest is deleted; 'A Trial of Archery' never unlocks, and Heavenly Shot becomes unobtainable on that save.

along_the_way: This is step one of the two-quest chain that gates the Archer maister skill Heavenly Shot. The skill itself comes from the follow-up quest, not this one.
gotchas: Elf-made bows are rejected — the game does not flag this clearly. Buy a human bow from a Vernworth vendor.

CONFLICT: Fextralife says the quest is 'not affected by the passage of time' once active and lists its cancellation trigger as unknown, but Fextralife's own master list places it in the Legacy deletion group. Read that as: no internal countdown, but a hard point of no return.

name: Home Is Where the Hearth Is
how_to_start: Return to occupied Melve after 'Trouble on the Cape' and speak with Lennart inside Ulrika's house. Getting into Melve requires bribing the gate guard (5,000G) or climbing the wall.
prerequisites: 'Readvent of Calamity' and 'Trouble on the Cape' completed. 'An Unsettling Encounter' is also cited by Fextralife. 'Brothers Brave and Timid' is optional but makes a step easier.
timing: After Trouble on the Cape, while Melve is under royal-army occupation.

missable.window: The whole Ulrika chain hangs off 'Readvent of Calamity', which is deleted when 'Feast of Deception' completes; Fextralife also flags this quest itself as time-limited (exact cutoff unstated).
missable.warning: If you finish Feast of Deception before starting the Melve/Ulrika chain, this quest and the Ulrika romance are gone for the run.

bring: 5,000 Gold for the Melve gate bribe (or be ready to climb the wall)
Four swords, if you would rather buy them than steal them

best_outcome.summary: Arm the villagers with four swords, beat back the soldiers alongside Lennart, then meet Ulrika at the Harve pier at night to complete her romance.
steps: Bribe or climb into occupied Melve and speak to Lennart in Ulrika's house.
Get four swords - if the brothers from 'Brothers Brave and Timid' are alive they distract the storeroom guard; otherwise buy four swords beforehand.
Give the swords to Lennart, then fight off the royal soldiers outside with the armed villagers.
Travel to Harve Village and report to Ulrika at the docks.
Return to the pier at night for the closing romance scene.

bad_outcome.summary: The chain is never started, or the villagers are left unarmed.
bad_outcome.how_it_happens: Finishing Feast of Deception before starting Readvent of Calamity/Trouble on the Cape, or failing to deliver swords.
bad_outcome.consequences: Ulrika's romance and this quest are permanently unavailable; no alternative route to the romance is confirmed.

along_the_way: Fextralife describes a second branch where the villagers arm themselves and fight for their own freedom, but does not document its steps or rewards.
gotchas: Sources conflict on missability: Game8's quest page says it is not missable, while Fextralife's quest page and master list flag it as time-limited. Fextralife's master list is treated as authoritative here.
No source states the exact in-game deadline for this quest on its own - the confirmed hard gate is the Readvent of Calamity chain being lost at Feast of Deception.
The 5,000G bribe can be skipped by climbing the wall, per player reports.
Multiple quest-blocking glitch reports exist around NPC placement; save before entering Melve.

name: House of the Blue Sunbright
how_to_start: Diana, a housemaid, stops you automatically near the stairs leading down to the Common Quarter / Slums in Vernworth.
prerequisites: Complete the side quest 'The Gift of Giving' first.
timing: After 'The Gift of Giving'. Completion requires waiting one in-game day partway through.
bring: 1x Misshapen Eye (Cyclops drop)
1x Detoxifying Decoction (500 G at Philbert's Sundries)
1x Waking Powder (400 G at Philbert's Sundries)

best_outcome.summary: Equip the manservant Sebastian with all three items so he survives the trip to Melve and brings back the Blue Sunbright himself.
steps: Talk to Diana by the Common Quarter stairs in Vernworth.
Follow the quest to Sebastian, who intends to fetch a Blue Sunbright flower from Melve for his mistress.
Before he leaves, give him all three items: Misshapen Eye, Detoxifying Decoction and Waking Powder.
Leave the manor and pass one in-game day.
Return to the manor to see the flower delivered and collect payment.
rewards: 2x Fine Harspud Roborant (PowerPyx; Game8 lists only the XP and gold)

bad_outcome.summary: Sebastian sets off unequipped and is ambushed in Melve.
bad_outcome.how_it_happens: Failing to hand over the three items before he departs.
bad_outcome.consequences: Sebastian is attacked by a hobgoblin in Melve and has to be rescued; the quest becomes a rescue run rather than a clean delivery. No source I reached confirms whether he can die outright.

along_the_way: The Misshapen Eye means a Cyclops hunt — the forest east of Vernworth is the nearest reliable spawn if you already spent yours on an upgrade.
Pairs naturally with 'A Case of Sculptor's Block', which also sends you past Cyclops territory.
gotchas: If you already consumed your Misshapen Eye on a weapon enhancement you must go kill another Cyclops.
The shop is written as 'Philbert's Sundries' by Game8 and 'Philnert's Sundries' by PowerPyx — same shop, spelling differs between sources.
The ending is a downer beat regardless of how well you prepare: the lady of the house comes downstairs and slaps the Arisen. Walk away before your pawns retaliate against her.
Rewards differ between sources: Game8 lists 900 XP / 3,000 G only; PowerPyx adds 2x Fine Harspud Roborant.

name: Hunt for the Jadeite Orb
how_to_start: Talk to either Offulve or Everard after arriving in Checkpoint Rest Town. Both want a Jadeite Orb, and each will commission you.
prerequisites: Reach Checkpoint Rest Town. The project brief places it after 'Feast of Deception'; no source I reached names a hard story prerequisite.
timing: Once you have access to Checkpoint Rest Town. No deadline reported by Game8 or Gamer Guides.
bring: 7,500 G to buy the genuine Jadeite Orb at Ibrahim's Scrap Store
2,000 G to have Ibrahim forge a copy
12,000 G spare only if you intend the bribe route (not recommended)

best_outcome.summary: Buy one real orb, have Ibrahim forge a fake, give the REAL one to Everard (who authenticates) and the FAKE to Offulve (who does not).
steps: Talk to Offulve and Everard in Checkpoint Rest Town to take on both commissions.
Buy the Jadeite Orb from Ibrahim's Scrap Store for 7,500 G.
Commission a forgery from Ibrahim for 2,000 G.
Hand the GENUINE orb to Everard — he inspects it and a fake gets you arrested.
Hand the FORGED orb to Offulve — he does not authenticate and accepts it.

bad_outcome.summary: Everard catches the forgery and you go to jail, or you buy your way out and lose most of the payout.
bad_outcome.how_it_happens: Giving the FAKE orb to Everard. He authenticates it and reports you.
bad_outcome.consequences: Jail time. If you instead pre-emptively bribe Ibrahim for 12,000 G to cover for you, you keep the Ring of Skullduggery but forfeit the gold reward — a net loss against the clean route.

along_the_way: Ibrahim's Scrap Store is the game's forger and the same shop that forges grimoires (6,000 G each) for 'The Sorcerer's Appraisal' — this quest is how most players learn the mechanic.
Doing this quest before the grimoire quests means you already know where to buy the forgeries Myrddin will accept.
gotchas: The orbs are not interchangeable: Everard authenticates, Offulve does not. Getting them the wrong way round is the whole trap.
The bribe route is strictly worse than just giving Everard the real orb — do not treat it as an equivalent branch.
Fextralife does NOT flag this quest (!), and neither Game8 nor Gamer Guides lists a time limit, so it is recorded as not missable.

name: Masked Correspondence
how_to_start: Speak with Sven in his chambers on the 2nd floor of Vernworth Castle (northwest corner) after completing 'Seat of the Sovran'. He gives you a letter to deliver at the masquerade.
prerequisites: Complete 'Seat of the Sovran'. You also need masquerade attire — the Eventide Mask (from 'The Stolen Throne') and the clothing from 'The Ornate Box'.
timing: Chapter 1 only, in the window between Seat of the Sovran and Feast of Deception.

missable.window: Deleted permanently when the main quest 'Feast of Deception' begins. It is one of the five side quests Fextralife's master list names as killed at that point.
missable.warning: Deliver Sven's letter to Lord Patrick before you trigger Feast of Deception — the quest is wiped the moment that main quest starts.

bring: Eventide Mask
Courtly/masquerade clothing from The Ornate Box

best_outcome.summary: Deliver Sven's letter to Lord Patrick at the masquerade and report back to Sven.
steps: Take the letter from Sven in his chambers.
Sleep at an inn if needed to advance to masquerade night, then attend at Vernworth Hall in full attire.
Find Lord Patrick — blue cape, black-and-gold mask.
Hand him the letter.
Return to Sven's chambers to report.

bad_outcome.summary: Quest silently vanishes.
bad_outcome.how_it_happens: Starting Feast of Deception with the quest unstarted or unfinished.
bad_outcome.consequences: Permanent loss of the XP, gold and Onyx. No follow-up quests are lost — this quest unlocks nothing.

along_the_way: You need the masquerade outfit for other Chapter 1 content anyway; get The Ornate Box and The Stolen Throne done first.
gotchas: Fextralife's quest page wording ('not missable initially') is misleading — the master list is unambiguous that Feast of Deception deletes it. Treat it as missable.
sources: Fextralife master side-quest list (Feast of Deception cutoff group)

name: Medicament Predicament
how_to_start: Speak to Flora outside Runne's Apothecary in Melve.
prerequisites: None beyond reaching Melve. PowerPyx additionally states the main quest 'Seat of the Sovran' must have been started; Fextralife lists no prerequisite.
timing: Early — available on your first or a return visit to Melve.
bring: A Fruit Roborant, or Dried Fruit plus Greenwarish or Morningtide to craft one, or 600 G to buy one

best_outcome.summary: Bring Flora a Fruit Roborant.
steps: Speak with Flora outside the apothecary and agree to help.
Buy a Fruit Roborant from the apothecary (600 G) or craft one from Dried Fruit + Greenwarish or Morningtide.
Return it to Flora at the same spot.
rewards: Later: Chirurgeon's Tome from Flora in Vernworth, unlocking the Chirurgeon pawn specialization

bad_outcome.summary: No distinct failure state is documented.
bad_outcome.how_it_happens: Fextralife states the quest has only one resolution path.
bad_outcome.consequences: Not documented.

along_the_way: The Chirurgeon pawn specialization (lets a pawn cure debilitations without items) comes from Flora later in Vernworth, not at quest turn-in — go find her again after she relocates.
gotchas: Not on any of Fextralife's three points-of-no-return lists, and PowerPyx records no missable flag — treated as safe.
CONFLICT on the prerequisite: PowerPyx requires 'Seat of the Sovran' started; Fextralife says none.
Fextralife notes the Chirurgeon's Tome arrives 'later'; a user comment there suggests it may be affinity-gated rather than a guaranteed quest reward. Unconfirmed.

name: Mercy Among Thieves
region: Vermund/Battahl border (Checkpoint Rest Town, Coral Snakes hideout)
how_to_start: SOURCES CONFLICT. Game8: speak to Tobias at the Vermund-Battahl Border Gate after completing 'Feast of Deception'. PowerPyx: it begins at Checkpoint Rest Town after crossing the border gate, with Lyssandro as quest giver, after feeding a boy near the inn twice and speaking to two men by the Oxcart Station.
prerequisites: Complete 'Feast of Deception'.
timing: Available once you reach the border/Checkpoint Rest Town post-Feast.

missable.window: Unavailable after completing the main quest 'Legacy' (Unmoored World transition).
missable.warning: BLUNT: this is on Game8's after-'Legacy' cutoff list. It is also the prerequisite for 'Off the Pilfered Path', which has its own kill-window where Hugo can die. Do this one early in the Battahl arc, not last.

bring: Full combat kit — multi-stage bandit fights
Do NOT plan on oxcart travel; oxcarts are disabled during this quest

best_outcome.summary: Track the Coral Snakes to their hideout, fight through with the guards, and resolve Hugo's fate.
steps: Feed the boy near the inn twice, then speak to the two men at the Oxcart Station.
Speak to Lyssandro, then gather information from survivors of the oxcart raid.
Travel south ON FOOT to locate the Coral Snakes' hideout.
Pursue Hugo through the cave, defeating bandits along the way.
Storm the deeper levels of the hideout with the guard reinforcements.

along_the_way: Loot chests are scattered throughout the hideout.
Directly sets up 'Off the Pilfered Path' with Hugo at the Bakbattahl Gaol.
gotchas: SOURCE CONFLICT on the quest giver and start location: Game8 says Tobias at the border gate, PowerPyx says Lyssandro at Checkpoint Rest Town. PowerPyx's own side-quest index also files this under Checkpoint Rest Town. Both may be true in sequence (border-gate hook, town quest-giver) — unresolved, verify in-game.
Oxcarts are disabled for the duration. Budget travel time.
Neither source documents a spare-or-kill dialogue choice for Hugo. Hugo's actual fate is decided later, in 'Off the Pilfered Path'.

name: Nesting Troubles
how_to_start: Speak with Lennart in Melve after the main quest 'In Dragon's Wake'. He asks for help clearing a saurian nest across the river.
prerequisites: Complete 'In Dragon's Wake' (Game8). Fextralife notes it stops appearing once you advance Brant's main quests far enough to trigger the dragon attack on Melve.
timing: Early Vermund, while Melve is intact.

missable.window: Closes permanently when the main quest 'Feast of Deception' is completed; Fextralife also notes the quest stops appearing once Brant's main quests trigger the dragon attack on Melve.
missable.warning: Clear the saurian nest for Lennart before you finish Feast of Deception - after that it is gone, and advancing Brant's main quests can remove it even earlier.

best_outcome.summary: Blow up the nest with explosive casks, then finish it with the single jar of poison - hitting the throw is the clean completion.
steps: Take the quest from Lennart in Melve.
Follow the marker to the explosive casks outside Melve.
Pick up casks and throw them across the river into the nest; repeat until the saurians are dead.
Report back to Lennart.
Pick up the jar of purple poison on the ground near Melve's entrance.
Throw it from the cliff edge into the nest - aim carefully, there is only one jar.
Return to Lennart.

bad_outcome.summary: You miss the poison-jar throw.
bad_outcome.how_it_happens: There is exactly one poison jar. A missed throw cannot be retried without reloading.
bad_outcome.consequences: The quest resolves on a lesser outcome rather than a clean success. Fextralife states the rewards are identical either way, so the loss is narrative rather than material.

gotchas: Save immediately before the poison throw - there is no second jar.

Fextralife's quest page does not label the quest time-limited, but its master list and Game8's missables list both put it behind the Feast of Deception wall. Fextralife also adds an earlier soft cutoff via Brant's main quests.
Community reports tie this quest to Fighter mastery skill access; that link is unverified by a primary guide.

name: Off the Pilfered Path
how_to_start: Speak to Hugo at the Bakbattahl Gaol entrance.
prerequisites: Complete the main quest 'Nation of the Lambent Flame' AND the side quest 'Mercy Among Thieves'.
timing: Battahl arc, after Mercy Among Thieves. Runs over several in-game days of paying Ekertt in instalments.

missable.window: Not a fixed clock, but there is a HARD FAIL STATE: if you do not wipe out the Coral Snakes at the Ancient Battleground yourself, Hugo goes after them and dies, failing the quest.
missable.warning: BLUNT: the 'optional' step is not optional. Kill the Coral Snakes at the Ancient Battleground YOURSELF before Hugo can try. If Hugo dies, the quest fails permanently.

bring: Combat kit for the Coral Snakes at the Ancient Battleground

best_outcome.summary: Buy Hugo's release in instalments AND clear the Coral Snakes yourself so he survives and leaves to make his own way.
steps: Speak to Brefft twice to learn about Hugo's parents and the Coral Snake hideout.
Talk to Hugo about his situation.
Consult Dietrich about getting Hugo released.
Pay Ekertt 1,000 G to start work on the release.
GO AND ELIMINATE THE CORAL SNAKES AT THE ANCIENT BATTLEGROUND YOURSELF.
Pay Ekertt 2,500 G, then 5,000 G, for Hugo's eventual release.
rewards: White-Leather Kerchief (on the 'Hugo departs independently' ending)

bad_outcome.summary: Hugo dies going after the Coral Snakes himself.
bad_outcome.how_it_happens: Leaving the Coral Snakes at the Ancient Battleground alive while progressing the release payments.
bad_outcome.consequences: Hugo is killed; the quest fails immediately and the reward is lost.

along_the_way: You can choose to tell Hugo what happened to his parents or stay silent.
The ending branches on 'Short-Sighted Ambition': if that quest ended negatively, Hugo ends up working at a shop; otherwise he sets off on his own (the kerchief ending).
gotchas: Single-source (PowerPyx) on the payment amounts and the Short-Sighted Ambition cross-link — medium confidence on the numbers, but the Hugo death condition is stated plainly.
This quest's outcome is entangled with a THIRD quest ('Short-Sighted Ambition'). If Julian cares about Hugo's ending, plan those two together.

name: One-Eyed Interloper
how_to_start: Triggers on the road in northern Vermund while you are travelling toward Vernworth with Gregor and his soldiers during the main quest 'In Dragon's Wake'. A Cyclops crashes into the party at a river crossing.
prerequisites: Be escorting / following Gregor during 'In Dragon's Wake'.
timing: Very early game, during the journey from Melve toward the capital.
bring: Curatives — the Cyclops hits hard at the level you meet it

best_outcome.summary: Kill the Cyclops that ambushes Gregor's party; Gregor then gives you the letter that gets you an audience in Vernworth.
steps: Follow Gregor's soldiers north toward Vernworth during 'In Dragon's Wake'.
At the river arena, attack the natural rock dam to release a torrent of water that knocks the Cyclops down.
Attack from behind, or climb its legs and back to reach the head, which is the weak point.
Topple it and focus the exposed head.
Once it is dead, speak to Gregor to receive the Missive to the Captain.
Continue to Vernworth on foot or by oxcart.
rewards: Missive to the Captain (grants an audience with Captain Brant in Vernworth)

along_the_way: The Misshapen Eye this Cyclops can drop is the same item 'House of the Blue Sunbright' later asks for — worth keeping rather than spending on an upgrade.
gotchas: Fextralife files this as a side quest, but it is functionally a scripted encounter inside the 'In Dragon's Wake' main quest; Game8 describes it as part of the main progression. Treat the 'side quest' label as a wiki categorisation, not a separate startable quest.

Insider Gaming reports no item loot from the fight itself, only the freedom to continue to Vernworth solo or by oxcart; Game8 reports 2,120 XP / 113 DCP. Both can be true (XP is not loot), but no single source lists a complete reward set.
The bad_outcome fields are left null on purpose — no source I reached describes a failure branch for this fight.

name: Ordeals of a New Recruit
how_to_start: Talk to Phill near the southern gate of Borderwatch Outpost.
timing: Immediate. This is a timed rescue.

missable.window: Immediate — no wandering. Exact number of in-game hours/days not documented by any source I found.
missable.warning: BLUNT: GO STRAIGHT THERE. Accardo DIES if you dawdle. This is one of the earliest quests in the game and one of the easiest to fail by treating it casually.

bring: Anti-harpy tools — ranged or wide-arc melee

best_outcome.summary: Reach Accardo south of Borderwatch Outpost immediately, kill the harpies, and report back to Phill.
steps: Head south of Borderwatch Outpost immediately.
Defeat the flock of harpies attacking Accardo.
Return to Borderwatch Outpost and report to Phill.

bad_outcome.summary: Arriving too late.
bad_outcome.how_it_happens: Not going immediately after taking the quest.
bad_outcome.consequences: Accardo dies. Quest failed.

along_the_way: Borderwatch Outpost is also where Beren is first met and where the training swords for 'Claw Them Into Shape' are sold.
gotchas: No source states the actual time window in in-game hours. Assume you have very little.
Rewards are trivial — this one is about not getting an NPC killed, not loot.

name: Out of the Forest, Into the Forge
how_to_start: Unlocks automatically on completing 'The Ailing Arborheart'. Report back to Doireann at Sacred Arbor to begin the active objectives. PowerPyx credits Sara in Bakbattahl as the trigger NPC.
prerequisites: Complete 'The Ailing Arborheart'.
timing: Immediately after The Ailing Arborheart; requires free movement between Sacred Arbor and Bakbattahl.

missable.window: Fextralife marks this time-limited with roughly 12 in-game days from start. It also specifically warns: do NOT activate the red beam in Bakbattahl while this is open — it passes a large block of time and makes the quest vanish outright.
missable.warning: You have about 12 in-game days once this starts, and the quest needs you to deliberately rot food for about a week — so start it only when you can commit, and do not touch the red beam in Bakbattahl until it is done.

bring: Fresh apples (buyable in Vernworth, or dropped by goblins) and fresh fish (from shallow water near Sacred Arbor) — to be left to spoil
The Ferrystone Doireann provides
NO pawn with the Logistician specialization
Stasis augment OFF

best_outcome.summary: Rot the ingredients, have Doireann cook nutriabh, use it to distract Brokkr, and harvest all six Scalecinder piles in Stragglers' Cave.
steps: Report to Doireann — Brokkr has the Scalecinder needed for the tree.
Acquire fresh apples and fresh fish, then rest days until both spoil into rotten apples and rotten fish in your inventory (about a week).
Give the spoiled ingredients to Doireann; she cooks the elven dish nutriabh.
Travel with Doireann to Brokkr's Smithy using the Ferrystone she gives you.
Follow Sara; she leads you to Stragglers' Cave where forge waste is dumped.

RUN AHEAD of Doireann into the cave — she triggers the exit when she reaches the midpoint, so getting ahead maximises your collection time. Gather all six piles of green Scalecinder powder while Brokkr is distracted.
Return the Scalecinder to Doireann at Sacred Arbor.
rewards: Port Crystal (given after returning to Sacred Arbor)

bad_outcome.summary: The quest silently vanishes, or you leave the cave with only part of the Scalecinder.
bad_outcome.how_it_happens: Activating the red beam in Bakbattahl while the quest is open; letting the ~12-day clock expire; or letting Doireann reach the cave midpoint before you have collected all six piles.
bad_outcome.consequences: Permanent loss of the Port Crystal — one of a very limited number in the game — plus 13,000 G and the Warbler Capelet.

along_the_way: A Logistician pawn will automatically craft your rotting food into something else and break the ingredient step. Dismiss it first.
The Stasis augment preserves food and will likewise stop the spoilage. Unequip it.
gotchas: SOURCE CONFLICT on missability: Fextralife flags this quest time-limited (~12 days, red-beam warning); PowerPyx describes no time limit at all and only warns about outrunning Doireann in the cave. Fextralife's (!) flag is the ground truth here, but the exact day count is single-sourced.
The Port Crystal reward is not mentioned by PowerPyx; it is on the Fextralife page only.

name: Oxcart Courier
how_to_start: Speak to Donovan at the Vernworth North Gate oxcart station. He asks you to carry a letter from Lady Margit to Ser Lennart in Melve. Donovan tends to be present in the morning; rest and return if he is absent.
prerequisites: Game8 lists the main quest 'In Dragon's Wake' as the gate; Fextralife lists none. You need 100 G for the oxcart fare.
timing: Early Chapter 1, while Lennart is still stationed in Melve.

missable.window: TWO independent closers. (1) Fextralife: the quest is cancelled before the main quest 'Readvent of Calamity' begins. (2) Ser Lennart eventually relocates from Melve to another village, after which the quest can no longer be started.
missable.warning: Do this in your first Vernworth stretch — it is cancelled once Readvent of Calamity starts, and Lennart leaves Melve before that anyway.

bring: 100 G oxcart fare
Gear for a possible monster raid on the oxcart

best_outcome.summary: Deliver Margit's letter to Ser Lennart in Melve and report back to Donovan.
steps: Board the Vernworth oxcart to Melve — oxcarts only depart in early morning. Pick 'Doze Off' to arrive faster.
Find Ser Lennart near the village well in Melve, in the morning. He wears a feathered cape and has a distinctive haircut.
Give him the letter.
Return to Donovan in Vernworth.

bad_outcome.summary: Quest is cancelled and cannot be restarted.
bad_outcome.how_it_happens: Letting Lennart leave Melve, or reaching Readvent of Calamity with the letter undelivered.
bad_outcome.consequences: Loss of the reward, and of the Nesting Troubles handoff (Nesting Troubles is itself deleted at Feast of Deception, so it must be done in the same early stretch).

along_the_way: Oxcart journeys can be ambushed mid-route; dozing off means you wake up to the fight already in progress.
gotchas: SOURCE CONFLICT on rewards: Fextralife says 400 XP / 500 G / Miner's Hosen; Game8 says 300 XP / 5,000 G. The 5,000 G figure is likely a typo but I could not confirm either way.
Some players report Lennart offers Nesting Troubles immediately, without needing this quest completed first.

name: Prey for the Pack
region: Vermund/border (Checkpoint Rest Town; Moonglow Flower Field; Putrid Cave)
how_to_start: Visit Morris at Checkpoint Rest Town. He asks you to find and save his son Rodge, taken by wolves.
prerequisites: Reach Checkpoint Rest Town.
timing: Timed — several in-game days. The timer ends when Rodge is rescued. The trail is followed AT NIGHT.

missable.window: Several in-game days from accepting it.
missable.warning: BLUNT: timed, and Rodge is a wolf's dinner if you sit on it. Game8's missables page lists Rodge among NPCs who die on failure. Go at night, with lantern oil, and do not put it off.

bring: Lantern Oil — the flower-petal trail is only followable at night
Anti-wolf pack kit

best_outcome.summary: Follow the glowing blue petal trail at night to the Putrid Cave, kill the wolves, and escort Rodge home.
steps: Talk to NPCs in town for clues pointing to Moonglow Flower Field.
Go to the field AT NIGHT with lantern oil.
Follow the piles of flowers / glowing blue petals further east.
Cross past the destroyed stone bridge to the Putrid Cave.
Kill the wolves and rescue Rodge.
Escort him safely back to town.

bad_outcome.summary: Running out the timer.
bad_outcome.how_it_happens: Not completing within the several-day window.
bad_outcome.consequences: Per Game8's missables page, Rodge dies. Gameranx does not confirm the death outcome explicitly — see gotchas.

along_the_way: Morris's permanent shop discount also cheapens the Ornate Box in 'The Ornate Box' via 'Medicament Predicament' — the apothecary economy is interlinked.
gotchas: SOURCE GAP: Gameranx explicitly does NOT confirm what happens if the timer expires. The 'Rodge dies' outcome comes from Game8's missables page only. Flagged as unverified.
Night-only trail. Daytime trips waste the timer.

name: Put a Spring in Thy Step
how_to_start: Travel south through Drabnir's Grotto onto Agamen Volcanic Island. Gautstafr, an elderly dwarf complaining about his back, is on the south path — speak to him.
prerequisites: Get through Drabnir's Grotto and reach Agamen Volcanic Island.
timing: Once you can reach Agamen Volcanic Island from Battahl.

missable.window: Permanently deleted on entering the Unmoored World via 'Legacy'. No internal countdown.
missable.warning: Do this before 'Legacy' — it is the only source of the Magick Archer maister skill Martyr's Bolt, and it also unlocks the Magick Archer vocation itself.

bring: Three wildflowers/herbs — Morningtide or Pitywort, both of which grow nearby
100 G if you want the hot spring trophy

best_outcome.summary: Fetch Gautstafr his flowers, then escort him safely to Geyser Hamlet and speak to Cliodhna twice.
steps: Collect three wildflowers (Morningtide or Pitywort).
Deliver them to Gautstafr where you met him.
Visit Windwalker's Home, north across shallow water on a small island, for the initial reward.
Escort Gautstafr to Geyser Hamlet, staying close and clearing enemies en route.
Speak with Cliodhna at the hot spring.
Talk to Cliodhna AGAIN afterwards to receive the Spellbow's Paradox, which unlocks the Magick Archer maister skill Martyr's Bolt.
rewards: Spellbow's Paradox → Martyr's Bolt (second Cliodhna conversation)

bad_outcome.summary: Gautstafr dies during the escort, or you enter the Unmoored World without finishing.
bad_outcome.how_it_happens: Leaving him exposed to volcanic-island enemies during the escort, or triggering 'Legacy' first.
bad_outcome.consequences: Losing the quest costs the Magick Archer vocation unlock and Martyr's Bolt. No source documents what specifically happens if Gautstafr dies mid-escort.

along_the_way: Gates the Magick Archer maister skill Martyr's Bolt (Cliodhna, Geyser Hamlet) — confirmed by Fextralife, and PowerPyx independently confirms the Spellbow's Paradox drop. Counts toward the 'Master of the Maisters' trophy.
Also unlocks the Magick Archer vocation.
Paying 100 G to use the hot spring gets the bronze trophy 'This'll Cure What Ails Ye'.
Gautstafr and Cliodhna reappear later as evacuees in 'The Importance of Aiding Ernesto' in the Unmoored World.
gotchas: CONFLICT on missability: PowerPyx explicitly calls this quest 'not missable', but Fextralife's master list places it in the 'Legacy' deletion group. PowerPyx most likely means there is no in-quest timer. Treat the Legacy cutoff as real.

The Martyr's Bolt tome comes from a SECOND conversation with Cliodhna after the quest completes — PowerPyx's page does not mention Cliodhna or Martyr's Bolt at all and only lists the Spellbow's Paradox as a reward. Do not walk away after the quest ends.
CONFLICT on flowers: Fextralife specifies wildflowers such as Morningtide; PowerPyx says any three herbs or wildflowers, recommending Pitywort.

name: Readvent of Calamity
how_to_start: Return to Melve Village after completing one of Captain Brant's Vernworth quests. A dragon attack event triggers.
prerequisites: Complete at least one of Captain Brant's Vernworth quests. Complete 'Scaly Invaders' before Ulrika will appear in Harve Village.
timing: After the coronation, before Brant finalises his plan.

missable.window: After completing one of Brant's quests and BEFORE completing 'Feast of Deception'.
missable.warning: BLUNT, HIGHEST PRIORITY IN VERMUND: this single quest gates the Mystic Spearhand vocation unlock AND the entire Ulrika romance. Complete Feast of Deception without it and both are gone for the save. Also: NPCs CAN PERMANENTLY DIE in the dragon attack, including ones other quests need. Carry a Wakestone before you go.

bring: A Wakestone — insurance against losing quest NPCs in the dragon attack
Ranged/anti-dragon kit

best_outcome.summary: Repel the dragon with the Melve NPCs intact, follow Ulrika's thread through to Harve, and report back to Lennart.
steps: Repel the dragon — do NOT try to kill it; it retreats at roughly half health.
Wait a day and return to Melve.
Stay overnight at Ulrika's house.
Find Ulrika in Harve Village (requires 'Scaly Invaders' done first).
Report on her wellbeing to Lennart in Melve.
Speak to Sigurd to unlock the Mystic Spearhand vocation.

bad_outcome.summary: Skipping the Melve dragon attack, or letting NPCs die in it.
bad_outcome.how_it_happens: Completing 'Feast of Deception' without having done this, or fighting the attack carelessly.
bad_outcome.consequences: Quest permanently unavailable; Ulrika will not appear in the later romance-related quests; Mystic Spearhand unlock path via this route is lost. Dead NPCs stay dead without a Wakestone.

along_the_way: 'Scaly Invaders' at Harve Village is a hard prerequisite for finding Ulrika — do it first.
gotchas: Half-health retreat: people waste the fight trying to kill the dragon.
Missable status corroborated by three sources (Game8 quest page, Game8 missables page, PowerPyx index).

name: Saint of the Slums
how_to_start: In Vernworth's Slums outside The Gracious Hand, listen to Vlasiy complaining about his son Lubomir's health, then speak to Elena after he leaves.
prerequisites: Access to The Gracious Hand in the Vernworth slums.
timing: Once you have free access to the Vernworth slums.

missable.window: Permanently deleted on entering the Unmoored World via 'Legacy'. Separately, after the quest resolves you have roughly 3 in-game days to save the patients before they die.
missable.warning: Finishing the quest is not the end — the patients at The Gracious Hand die within about three days unless you go pay Radcliff at Checkpoint Rest Town to treat them.

bring: 3 Miasmite (dropped by Phantoms, which only spawn at night)
About 3,000 G for Radcliff's post-quest treatment

best_outcome.summary: Gather full evidence, get Elena arrested with a solid case, then pay Radcliff to save Lubomir and the other patients.
steps: Give Elena 3 Miasmite.
Follow Elena on her rounds.
Enter The Gracious Hand basement at night and take Records of Treatment and Unlabeled Medicine.
Interview the recovered patients Bruno and Jehan at Walter's Tavern.
Witness Elena's night meeting with Alois in the Common Quarter.
Take the medicine to Radcliff at Checkpoint Rest Town; wait one day for his analysis and return.
Apprehend Elena when she returns to The Gracious Hand.
AFTER completion: go back to Radcliff and pay him (~3,000 G) to treat the patients before they die.
rewards: Lubomir and the other patients survive (only if you pay Radcliff in time)

bad_outcome.summary: Elena escapes, or she is arrested on thin evidence, or the patients die.
bad_outcome.how_it_happens: Confronting Elena without the full evidence set; letting her see you gathering it, in which case she flees; or finishing the quest and never returning to Radcliff.
bad_outcome.consequences: Insufficient evidence leaves her conviction uncertain. If she flees, she escapes the quest entirely. Independently, Lubomir and the other patients die within ~3 days of completion if unaided.

along_the_way: Phantoms for Miasmite only spawn at night — plan to farm them in one night run rather than waiting on random encounters.
The basement is only accessible at night.
gotchas: CONFLICT on the timer: Fextralife says Lubomir can die if you delay too long AFTER STARTING the quest and that timing is critical throughout. PowerPyx says the quest itself has no strict time limit and that the ~3-day patient death clock begins only AFTER completion. The safe read is to treat both phases as urgent.
The post-quest Radcliff payment is easy to miss entirely — the quest shows as complete and nothing prompts you.
On Fextralife's master list this is one of the quests deleted by 'Legacy'.

name: Scaly Invaders
how_to_start: Fyoran approaches you in Harve Village on your second visit - Game8 ties this to exiting Stormwind Cave; Fextralife simply says returning to Harve a second time.
prerequisites: Reach Harve Village a second time. Game8 lists the 'Monster Culling' story quest as a prerequisite; Fextralife's comments dispute whether it is strictly required.
timing: Vermund mid-early game, before the Ulrika/Harve chain ('Trouble on the Cape' lists it as a prerequisite).

best_outcome.summary: Clear two waves of saurians from Harve Village with no villager casualties, letting the village rebuild.
steps: Accept Fyoran's request in Harve Village.
Kill every saurian in the village - cutting their tails weakens them.
Report to Fyoran in the town centre.
Leave Harve and let 2-3 in-game days pass so the villagers can repair.
Return; Fyoran and chief Jonas meet you and a second wave attacks.
Clear the second wave fast - villagers join in and can die.
Report to Fyoran for the closing cutscene.

bad_outcome.summary: Villagers die in the second wave.
bad_outcome.how_it_happens: Villagers fight alongside you in the second assault; slow clears get them killed.
bad_outcome.consequences: Not documented as a hard failure branch by any source - the guidance is simply to kill enemies quickly to avoid casualties.

gotchas: Fextralife's page and comments report NPCs vanishing before completion, leaving the quest unfinishable in some playthroughs; Gamerant also flags a bug. Treat this as a save-first quest.
Sources conflict on whether 'Monster Culling' is a hard prerequisite.
Fextralife explicitly marks this quest 'Time Limited: No', and it does not appear on Game8's missables list or Fextralife's master list of time-sensitive quests.

name: Shadowed Prayers
how_to_start: Speak to Menella at Flamebearer Palace in Bakbattahl.
prerequisites: Complete the main quest 'Nation of the Lambent Flame'.
timing: You must be at Flamebearer Palace IN THE MORNING for the Empress's prayer. Listed as a timed quest by dotesports.

missable.window: Flagged as a timed quest; the prayer scene is a morning-only window and the quest segment fails outright if you grab the wrong person.
missable.warning: BLUNT: this is a one-shot identification with a fail state. SAVE at the inn immediately before the prayer scene. Picking the wrong person fails that segment and your only recovery is a reload.

bring: A fresh save at the nearby inn — non-negotiable

best_outcome.summary: Correctly identify and apprehend the real assassin during the Empress's prayer.
steps: Arrive at Flamebearer Palace in the MORNING.
During the Empress's prayer, look for a man with his hair tied back and a wound on his RIGHT arm — a dark blue robe with a faint red band around the right arm.
Apprehend that person (R2 on PlayStation).

bad_outcome.summary: Grabbing the wrong worshipper.
bad_outcome.how_it_happens: Apprehending anyone other than the tied-back-hair man with the right-arm wound / red arm band.
bad_outcome.consequences: That quest segment fails. Recovery is reloading a save from the nearby inn.

along_the_way: Completing this unlocks 'A Candle in the Storm' from Menella.
gotchas: SOURCE CONFLICT: dotesports lists Shadowed Prayers among DD2's timed quests, while Game8's quest page does not state a time limit. Treat it as timed and do not sit on it.
The visual tell (red band on the right arm) is subtle at distance — get close before committing.

name: Shepherd of the Pawns
how_to_start: In the Unmoored World, travel to the Excavation Site on Agamen Volcanic Island. Help Henrique defeat the stone construct / Magick Golem at the gate, then speak with him.
prerequisites: Have started the Unmoored World quest 'Halls of the First Dawn'.
timing: Unmoored World only, after Halls of the First Dawn is underway.

missable.warning: Not individually flagged missable, but the Unmoored World consumes regions in the brine on a rolling timer — if Agamen Volcanic Island is swallowed before you get there, the quest goes with it.

bring: Combat gear for a Magick Golem / stone construct
Wakestones if you are managing the Unmoored World region timer

best_outcome.summary: Remove the Diminished Godsway's influence so the trapped pawns can leave, completing the evacuation.
steps: Fight the stone construct at the Excavation Site gate alongside Henrique and pick up its drops.
Speak to Henrique; he gives you the Overseer's Lodge Key.
Return to the gate area and unlock the second hut on the hill (PowerPyx) / the lodge behind the inn (Fextralife).
Take the Diminished Godsway staff from inside.
Bring it back to Henrique at the gaol.

bad_outcome.summary: No documented failure branch; the risk is the Unmoored World clock, not a player choice.
bad_outcome.how_it_happens: Letting the brine claim Agamen Volcanic Island before starting or finishing it; or hitting the documented Henrique-gets-stuck bug.
bad_outcome.consequences: Loss of a very large Unmoored World XP/gold/Wyrmslife Crystal payout.

along_the_way: ALTERNATE SOLUTION (Fextralife): instead of retrieving the Godsway, you can hire every trapped pawn and escort them to the nearby Riftstone. After several trips they dismiss themselves and the rewards are identical.
Some pawns will not leave at all until the Godsway's influence is removed, so the escort route is slower and only partly viable on its own.
gotchas: Fextralife explicitly states the cancellation conditions for this quest are UNKNOWN, while saying it is not time-limited. Given the Unmoored World's region-by-region brine consumption, treat 'not missable' as provisional.
Henrique is documented as sometimes becoming stuck or unresponsive. Reloading an earlier save is the only reported remedy.
SOURCE CONFLICT on the lodge location: Fextralife says the lodge behind the inn; PowerPyx says the second hut on the hill by the gate. Likely the same building described differently, but unconfirmed.

name: Short-Sighted Ambition
how_to_start: Buy anything from Isaac at Isaac's Wares in Bakbattahl's Mercantile Ward; he then asks you to fetch a Ripened Quince for his failing eyesight.
prerequisites: Reach Bakbattahl (normally via 'Nation of Lambent Flame'). Fextralife notes player reports that the main quest may not be strictly required.
timing: Any time after reaching Bakbattahl. The quest has built-in waiting - the quince needs about 3.5 in-game days to ripen.
bring: About 2,000-2,400 Gold for the second grimoire volume or its forgery

best_outcome.summary: Give Isaac a forged copy of 'On the Transference of Souls 2' - his family survives and he pays you handsomely.
steps: Buy something from Isaac to start the quest.
Pick a quince from the trees by the river south-west of Bakbattahl and let it ripen ~3.5 in-game days (rest/camp to pass time).
Give Isaac the Ripened Quince; return after a day for the next objective.
Go to Ibrahim's Scrap Store and arrange a FORGED copy of 'On the Transference of Souls 2' rather than handing over the genuine volume.
Give Isaac the forgery.
rewards: A grimoire that teaches a spell; Isaac later sells volume one, and the two volumes can be combined into the one-use 'Celestial Paean'

bad_outcome.summary: Give Isaac the genuine 'On the Transference of Souls 2'.
bad_outcome.how_it_happens: Handing over the real second volume instead of Ibrahim's forgery.
bad_outcome.consequences: Isaac reads it and performs the ritual; his wife and daughter die. You get 3,000 XP and the Ring of Disfavor, looted from the daughter's body, instead of the gold. Fextralife notes this branch opens a job for Hugo in a related quest.

gotchas: Game8 states this becomes available after 'Legacy'; every other source places it in normal Bakbattahl play after 'Nation of Lambent Flame'. Game8's claim looks wrong - Legacy is a point of no return - but it is recorded here rather than resolved.
Sources conflict on cost: Game8 says the genuine volume is 2,000G at Ibrahim's; Fextralife says the forged copy costs 2,400G.
The quince must actually ripen - handing over an unripe one does nothing.

name: Spellbound
how_to_start: Speak to Trysha at Eini's Home, in the forest north of Melve, after the main quest 'In Dragon's Wake'. She asks you to find grimoires so she can learn magick.
prerequisites: Complete the main quest 'In Dragon's Wake'. One of the five grimoires ('Towering Earth') additionally requires completing 'The Caged Magistrate'. Entering Myrddin's home in Checkpoint Rest Town to grab 'Let There Be Light' requires the Courtly Tunic and Breeches disguise.
timing: Available from early-to-mid game once 'In Dragon's Wake' is done; collecting all five grimoires spans Vermund and Checkpoint Rest Town.

missable.window: Permanently lost once you trigger 'Legacy' and enter the Unmoored World. Fextralife's master list names Spellbound among the quests deleted at Legacy.
missable.warning: Finish Spellbound before you start 'Legacy' — entering the Unmoored World deletes it along with the Meteoron and Celestial Paean Maister teachings it is the only source of.

bring: Courtly Tunic and Breeches (to enter Myrddin's home for 'Let There Be Light')
5,000 G for the Fulminous Shield grimoire in Melve
Gold for forgeries if you intend to satisfy Myrddin too (6,000 G per forged book at Ibrahim's Scrap Store)

best_outcome.summary: Bring Trysha GENUINE grimoires, ride out her magical outburst without killing her, and collect the Sorcerer and Mage Maister teachings.
steps: Talk to Trysha at Eini's Home north of Melve.

Collect the grimoires: 'Let There Be Light' on a table in Myrddin's study in Checkpoint Rest Town; 'Fulminous Shield' from the merchant in ruined Melve for 5,000 G; 'Nation's Death Knell' on the altar on the Ancient Battleground's second floor; 'Howling Blizzard' from the lit chest on Waterfall Cave's second floor (spawns a Lich); 'Towering Earth' from Waldhar in the Vernworth Slums ruins / The Gracious Hands' Vaults after 'The Caged Magistrate'.
Hand the GENUINE books to Trysha — never forgeries.
Pass several in-game days and return.
Trysha loses control of her magick. Do NOT kill her: dodge and outlast her spells until she tires, then physically subdue her.
Pass one more day to trigger the closing cutscene.
rewards: Conjurer's Jotting — Maister teaching for Meteoron (Sorcerer), from Trysha
Celestial Paean Maister teaching (Mage), from Eini

bad_outcome.summary: Trysha is given forged grimoires, or the quest is abandoned, and the Maister teachings are lost for the playthrough.
bad_outcome.how_it_happens: Handing Trysha forgeries bought from Ibrahim instead of the real books — or simply entering the Unmoored World with the quest unfinished.
bad_outcome.consequences: Game8 states that giving Trysha forged copies locks you out of key rewards including Celestial Paean. Losing the quest at Legacy means Meteoron and Celestial Paean cannot be obtained at all in that playthrough.

along_the_way: The Waterfall Cave grimoire chest spawns a Lich — come prepared.
The Ancient Battleground is northeast of Checkpoint Rest Town, reached by a ladder and a cave descent.
Ibrahim's Scrap Store in Checkpoint Rest Town is the same forger used by 'Hunt for the Jadeite Orb', which is how most players are introduced to the forgery mechanic.
gotchas: THE MAISTER FORK — the two quests want opposite things. Trysha ('Spellbound') requires GENUINE grimoires and rewards Meteoron (Sorcerer) plus Celestial Paean (Mage). Myrddin ('The Sorcerer's Appraisal') will accept FORGED grimoires without penalty and rewards Myrddin's Chronicle, the Maister teaching for Maelstrom. The play that gets you all three spells in one run is: buy forgeries at Ibrahim's Scrap Store, give the FAKES to Myrddin, and keep the REAL books for Trysha.
Forgeries cost 6,000 G each at Ibrahim's Scrap Store in Checkpoint Rest Town (RPG Site; PowerPyx confirms the same shop and price). Five forgeries is 30,000 G.

SOURCES CONFLICT on how many books each NPC needs. Game8's Spellbound page says Trysha needs all five genuine grimoires. PowerPyx says to give each quest-giver only three books and lists six obtainable grimoires (including two copies of 'Nation's Death Knell'). Windows Central likewise says Myrddin accepts three. Game8's Sorcerer's Appraisal page says you get Myrddin's full rewards from three forgeries. Because the counts do not agree, the safe play is to collect every genuine grimoire you can and give Trysha genuine ones only.

SOURCES CONFLICT on grimoire locations too: Game8 places 'Nation's Death Knell' on the Ancient Battleground altar and 'Howling Blizzard' in Waterfall Cave; PowerPyx puts a copy of 'Nation's Death Knell' in the SAME Waterfall Cave chest as 'Howling Blizzard' and a second copy at the Ancient Battleground. Check both spots.
Do not kill Trysha during her outburst — the quest resolves by outlasting and subduing her.

name: Steeled Resolve, Blazing Forge
how_to_start: Begins immediately at Brokkr's Smithy in Bakbattahl after you deliver the sword to Sara at the end of 'Dulled Steel, Cold Forge'.
prerequisites: Complete the side quest 'Dulled Steel, Cold Forge' (given by Roman in Vernworth).
timing: Directly after 'Dulled Steel, Cold Forge'. Progression needs you to leave and rest (a bench outside the Inn works) between scenes at the smithy.

missable.window: Permanently lost once you trigger 'Legacy' and enter the Unmoored World. Its hard prerequisite 'Dulled Steel, Cold Forge' is named on Fextralife's Legacy deletion list, so this follow-up cannot be started or finished afterwards. Fextralife also flags this quest (!) directly.
missable.warning: This is the back half of the Roman/Sara chain — finish both 'Dulled Steel, Cold Forge' and this before you start 'Legacy', or the whole chain and its 35,000 G are gone.

bring: Combat readiness for the Mountain Base Cave route to the forge
Nothing quest-specific

best_outcome.summary: Find Sara at the hidden forge, see the reforging through, and carry the news back to Roman in Vernworth.
steps: Complete 'Dulled Steel, Cold Forge' and hand the sword to Sara at Brokkr's Smithy in Bakbattahl.
Leave and rest (bench outside the Inn) to advance time, then return to the smithy to trigger the next scene with Brokkr.
Follow the trail to the forge via Mountain Base Cave, clearing enemies on the way in.
Find Sara safe at the forge and complete the reforging.
Fight your way back out — the return trip is easier if you cleared on the way in.
Return to Roman in Vernworth to report.

bad_outcome.summary: The chain is lost at Legacy.
bad_outcome.how_it_happens: Entering the Unmoored World with 'Dulled Steel, Cold Forge' or this follow-up unfinished.
bad_outcome.consequences: Both quests vanish permanently, forfeiting 6,000 XP and 35,000 G here plus whatever 'Dulled Steel, Cold Forge' pays. No in-quest failure branch is documented by any source I reached — PowerPyx describes it as linear with no failure conditions.

along_the_way: The Mountain Base Cave route is a dungeon crawl worth looting on the way through.
gotchas: You must leave the smithy and rest to advance dialogue — standing there talking will not progress it.
Clear enemies on the way IN to the forge; PowerPyx notes the exit is painless if you did and messy if you did not.
A PowerPyx commenter reports the palace door being sealed, blocking their route to Mountain Base Cave; the guide offers no alternative entry. If you hit this, the workaround is unsourced.

PowerPyx lists no time limit for this quest; the missable flag here rests on Fextralife's (!) plus the fact that its prerequisite is on the Legacy deletion list. The chain-deletion reasoning is an inference, clearly marked.
sources: Fextralife master side-quest list (points-of-no-return table) — supplied as project ground truth; page itself robots-blocked to fetch

name: Tensions on the Highroad
how_to_start: After completing 'Welcome to Battahl', return to the Oxcart Station at Vernworth's north gate and speak to Simon. He patrols, so if he is not at the station check the fountain steps near the Pawn Guild.
prerequisites: Complete 'Welcome to Battahl' and reach Bakbattahl for the first time.
timing: After first reaching Bakbattahl, before the main quest 'A New Godsway'.

missable.window: Permanently deleted by the main quest 'A New Godsway', which also deletes its own prerequisite 'Welcome to Battahl'.
missable.warning: Do this before 'A New Godsway' — that main quest wipes both this and 'Welcome to Battahl' off your log for good.

bring: Escort Letter (given by Simon)
Gear for a long cave section — you are separated from your pawns partway through

best_outcome.summary: Escort the oxcart, then follow Raghnall into Guerco Cavern and get back out.
steps: Take the escort instructions and Escort Letter from Simon.
Travel to the marked spot north of Checkpoint Rest Town and meet Ser Augustin's oxcart.
When Raghnall confronts the soldiers, pick a side (it does not change the result).
Follow Raghnall and Ser Augustin into Guerco Cavern.
Survive the floor collapse, which separates you from your pawns, and navigate the cave.
Find an exit the following day as Raghnall becomes trapped.

bad_outcome.summary: No branching failure outcome is documented — both sources say the quest resolves identically either way.
bad_outcome.how_it_happens: The only loss state is triggering 'A New Godsway' before finishing it.
bad_outcome.consequences: Quest deleted permanently; 4,000 XP and 12,000 G lost on that save.

along_the_way: You lose your pawns for the Guerco Cavern stretch — go in with your own healing and light, not the party's.
gotchas: CONFLICT on the choice: Fextralife says siding with Raghnall is recommended and that siding with the soldiers affects his affinity; PowerPyx says the choice has no effect at all. Nobody documents a concrete consequence, so treat the affinity claim as unverified.
Fextralife's own quest page lists the cancellation trigger as unknown ('??') even though its master list puts this in the 'A New Godsway' deletion group. Trust the master list.

name: The Ailing Arborheart
how_to_start: Go to The Arborheart in Sacred Arbor. Doireann speaks to you automatically; talk to her again at the railing in front of the great tree to formally begin.
prerequisites: Complete 'A Trial of Archery'. PowerPyx also lists 'Steeled Resolve, Blazing Forge' as required; Fextralife calls it recommended but not strictly required. Completion requires access to Battahl.
timing: After A Trial of Archery, once Sacred Arbor is open and Bakbattahl is reachable.
bring: A pawn with the Woodland Wordsmith specialization (optional, skips a lookup step)

best_outcome.summary: Learn that 'gwyfencha' means Scalecinder, then consult a Battahli blacksmith — which hands off directly into Out of the Forest, Into the Forge.
steps: Objective 1 — find out what gwyfencha means. Any of: carry a pawn with Woodland Wordsmith; ask Glyndwr, Doireann's brother; or complete 'Put a Spring in Thy Step' and ask Gautstafr. The answer is Scalecinder.
Objective 2 — travel to Brokkr's Smithy in Bakbattahl and speak with Sara, the apprentice.
Sara explains how Scalecinder is obtained and mentions an elven dish that might sway her employer. Quest completes and immediately triggers 'Out of the Forest, Into the Forge'.
rewards: Unlocks 'Out of the Forest, Into the Forge'

bad_outcome.summary: No branching outcome exists.

along_the_way: This is the entry point to the Sacred Arbor / Scalecinder chain; the payoff (Port Crystal, 13,000 G, Warbler Capelet) is in the follow-up, not here.
gotchas: SOURCE CONFLICT on the Warbler Capelet: Fextralife's Ailing Arborheart page lists it as a reward here ('reportedly'); PowerPyx lists only 1,600 XP here and puts the Capelet on Out of the Forest, Into the Forge. PowerPyx is more likely correct.
SOURCE CONFLICT on prerequisites: PowerPyx requires Steeled Resolve, Blazing Forge; Fextralife only recommends it.
Fextralife states the quest is not affected by time passage — but the follow-up it triggers IS on a ~12-day clock, so do not start this until you can act on it.

name: The Arisen's Shadow
how_to_start: Speak to Captain Brant at the Stardrop Inn at night after completing several of his quests, and exhaust his dialogue until he mentions someone stalking you.
prerequisites: Complete a few of Captain Brant's quests.
timing: The 'refuse' path requires waiting 3 in-game days before returning to Brant.

missable.window: Unavailable after completing the main quest 'Feast of Deception'.
missable.warning: BLUNT: on the pre-Feast cutoff list per both Game8's missables page and PowerPyx's index. The 'refuse' ending needs a 3-day wait afterwards, so start it with headroom before Feast of Deception — not the night before.

bring: A Wakestone — you can easily kill Bermudo by accident and need him alive

best_outcome.summary: Subdue Bermudo without killing him, refuse his bribe, let Brant take him into custody, then return after 3 days.
steps: Roam Vernworth until a hooded man, Bermudo, attacks you.
Catch or chase him down. Do NOT overkill him.
Refuse his offer of compensation.
He attacks; Brant intervenes and takes him into custody.
Wait 3 in-game days, then speak to Brant at the inn.

bad_outcome.summary: Taking the hush money, or killing Bermudo outright.
bad_outcome.how_it_happens: Demanding compensation ends the quest immediately for 5,000 G with Bermudo escaping. Excessive damage kills him outright.
bad_outcome.consequences: Compensation path: quest ends early, Bermudo escapes, no Brant resolution. Killing him: you must revive him with a Wakestone — if the body has vanished, check the Morgue.

gotchas: More gold (5,000 G) on the 'demand compensation' path than the 4,000 G proper ending — the greedy choice pays better but closes the story.
Bermudo dying is a common accident. Carry a Wakestone.

name: The Gift of Giving
how_to_start: Speak to Daphne on the path leading down to The Slums from the Common Quarter steps in Vernworth.
prerequisites: Reach the Vernworth Slums. PowerPyx additionally requires the main quest 'In Dragon's Wake' to be complete; Fextralife lists only slum access.
timing: Once the Vernworth Slums are accessible.

missable.window: Permanently deleted on entering the Unmoored World via 'Legacy'. No internal countdown.
missable.warning: There is no in-quest timer but the quest spans several in-game days of fetch steps, so start it well before 'Legacy' or you lose it mid-chain.

bring: Sunbloom and Noonbloom (to make a Bunch of Flowers)
1 Silver Ore
2 Gold Ore
